step-1.text: Lay one side panel flat, holes facing up. Screw in four cam pins and tap in four wood dowels.

count-1.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 4 cam pins and 4 wood dowels.

step-2.text: Slide the bottom panel onto the pins at the low end. Two cam locks go in, arrow toward the pin, then a firm clockwise turn.

count-2.text: This step uses 1 bottom panel and 2 cam locks.

step-3.text: Same move at the other end. Push the top panel onto its pins, add two cam locks, and turn them clockwise.

count-3.text: This step uses 1 top panel and 2 cam locks.

step-4.text: Pins and dowels go into the ends of the panels on this side too. With a helper, lower the second side onto all of them at once, then lock the last four cam locks.

count-4.text: This step uses 1 side panel, 4 cam pins, 4 wood dowels and 4 cam locks.

step-5.text: Tap four dowels into the ends of the plinth board and press it in under the bottom panel, at the front.

count-5.text: This step uses 1 plinth and 4 wood dowels.

step-6.text: Roll the wardrobe over so it lies on its front. Ask your helper, and put the flattened box underneath to save the finish.

count-6.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-7.text: Lay the back panel on, smooth side facing in. Line it up with the bottom corners and nail it along the edges, about every twenty centimeters. If the corners line up, the wardrobe is square.

step-8.text: Second back piece, butted tight against the first. Same nailing pattern along every edge.

step-9.text: Stand it up together. Lift with your legs, not your back.

count-9.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-10.text: The shelf above the rail goes in first, high up. Push four shelf pins into the holes at the height you want for each shelf, four pins in all, then rest the shelves on them, front edge flush.

count-10.text: This step uses 1 shelf and 4 shelf pins.

step-11.text: Screw a rail holder to each side of the hanging space, level with each other, then drop the clothes rail into the holders. Hang one coat and check it slides freely.

count-11.text: This step uses 1 clothes rail, 2 rail holders and 4 screws.

step-12.text: Press four hinges into the round cups on the back of each door, eight in all, then clip each door onto its mounting plates inside the frame. Doors this tall need a second pair of hands.

count-12.text: This step uses 2 doors, 8 hinges and 16 screws.

step-13.text: Shut the doors and check the lines. Tall doors drift, so nudge the hinge screws a quarter turn at a time until every gap matches.

count-13.text: Nothing new this step. Just you and the frame.

step-14.text: A handle for each door, on the side away from the hinges, about chest height. One screw from the inside.

step-15.text: Before anything goes inside, anchor it. Screw the wall bracket to the back edge of the top and into the wall with the right fixings for your wall. Tall, deep and heavy means it must be anchored.

done.text: Done. Your RAKKESTAD wardrobe with 2 doors is built. Give it a proud little pat.
